source.title: ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
source.authors: Thomas C. Bachlechner; Bodhisattwa Prasad Majumder; H. H. Mao; Gary Cottrell; Julian McAuley

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Compares architectures and initialization choices using training loss, convergence speed, and convergence failures; it does not directly measure training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 training-loss comparisons and CIFAR-10 ResNet training losses, plus Transformer convergence results. Its claims about 10,000-layer fully connected networks and dynamical isometry are not accompanied here by a directly extractable training-error result. Prior-work results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Table 2 reports the authors' own Fixup experiments: normalization-free ResNets attain low training loss and reach 80% accuracy faster than standard ResNets. These results bear on the Fixup clauses of V3 and V6. The extracted ReZero rows do not directly test the specified versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that ReZero improves signal propagation and convergence across fully connected networks, ResNets, and Transformers, and enables deep Transformer training. The reported deepest Transformer is 128 layers, despite the abstract's reference to 120.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a zero-initialized trainable scalar to each residual branch; tests CIFAR-10 classification loss and language-model convergence rather than the versions' original training-error measures.
record.method_sensitivity: ReZero residual-weight initialization (α=0 versus α=1) changes Transformer convergence; adding residual connections without normalization decreased convergence speed relative to plain FC in the reported CIFAR-10 experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: ReZero accelerates fitting in 32-layer fully connected networks; ordinary residual connections without normalization slow fitting in this experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zero-initialized residual gates can accelerate fully connected network optimization relative to plain, residual, and LayerNorm alternatives.

fits_no_version.finding: ReZero lowers training loss in four CIFAR-10 ResNet configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding zero-initialized trainable residual gates can improve final ResNet training loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero versus unit initialization of residual gates improves 12-layer Transformer convergence speed and enables convergence at 64 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-gate initialization affects Transformer convergence speed and trainable depth.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence (UAI), 2020
record.problems: The CIFAR-10 fully connected comparison is described as a simple experiment and Figure 3 does not provide recoverable per-architecture numbers in the supplied text. Training-loss values are not training classification-error measurements. Deep Transformer experiments are limited to the reported configurations and training cap.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying outcomes omitted. Cited results from other papers and the stated 10,000-layer fully connected claim are not included as rows because this paper does not provide corresponding result values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Training classification error, corrupted or random labels, CIFAR-100, and the specified size and training-recipe qualifications.
All: no two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum experiment.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, its prevention by identity shortcuts, longer-training controls, and special initialization of deep plain tanh networks.
All specified plain-network initialization comparisons, including activation matching, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional training.
All: no measured initial stability threshold, curvature trajectory, or edge-of-stability experiment. The one-cycle learning-rate recipe alone does not test this version.
Adding batch normalization to otherwise matched networks, higher-learning-rate tolerance, and a direct quantitative comparison of Fixup training stability.

missing.what: The authors' Fixup training-loss results: ResNet-56, 4.6 ± 0.2 versus standard 5.9 ± 0.1; ResNet-110, 3.3 ± 0.5 versus standard 4.0 ± 0.1, all in units of loss ×1000. These are experimental results, not merely cited findings.
missing.locator: Table 2; Appendix D.5 describes normalization-free Fixup; Appendix E.1 gives the training recipe

missing.what: Fixup epochs to 80% accuracy: ResNet-56, 13 ± 1 versus standard 20 ± 1; ResNet-110, 15 ± 1 versus standard 23 ± 4. Uncertainties are standard errors.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Verdicts rely on omitted Fixup results in the supplied text; the existing ReZero rows support related claims outside the versions' specified scope.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, or comparisons involving smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or spurious-local-minimum outcome.

Does not compare plain batch-normalized convolutional networks with the same networks using identity shortcuts across depth, or test the stated ImageNet and CIFAR-10 training-error pattern. ReZero gates residual branches and the reported outcomes are principally loss, convergence speed, and language-model BPB. The FixUp comparison is not a direct test of whether residual networks can train without normalization.

Tests zero versus unit initialization of ReZero residual weights, but not the listed activation-matched initializations, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, or 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
Does not compare batch normalization against the same networks without it in the stated MNIST, CIFAR-10 VGG, or ImageNet Inception settings.

rows.subject: FC + ReZero (6)
rows.operation_detail: Trained supervised image classification and compared training-loss convergence across four fully connected architectures.
rows.value: Converges to fit the training data between 7 and 15 times faster than other techniques
rows.note: The text reports an aggregate speed range across comparisons; it does not give per-comparator values in the supplied figure text.
rows.check: Measures the proposed ReZero method's speed in fully connected networks, without the plain batch-normalized convolutional depth comparison specified by V3. Figure 3 is discussed in Section 4, not Section 5.

rows.subject: FC + Res (2)
rows.operation_detail: Trained supervised image classification and compared training-loss convergence.
rows.measure: Training-loss convergence relative to plain fully connected network
rows.value: Without an additional normalization layer the residual connection decreases convergence speed compared to a plain fully connected network
rows.note: The paper states this direction explicitly but supplies no numerical relative speed for this pair.
rows.check: Slower convergence of an unnormalized residual fully connected network does not reverse V3's claim about training error across depths in batch-normalized convolutional networks. The discussion is in Section 4.
